title: Acute Visual Loss: The Clinical Triage Masterclass
summary: Sudden loss of vision (SLOV) is a high-stakes ophthalmic emergency defined by vision loss occurring within seconds to 24 hours. This guide provides a systematic approach to differentiating painful from painless etiologies to ensure sight-saving and life-saving interventions.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Temporal Triage
sections.content: Sudden Vision Loss (SLOV) describes a subjective decrease in vision reaching its peak within 24 hours. The primary clinical bifurcation is based on the presence or absence of PAIN. Painless loss suggests vascular, retinal, or neuro-ophthalmic causes, while painful loss often points to the anterior segment, glaucoma, or inflammatory processes.

branches: Painless: Retinal (RD, Vitreous Heme, Wet AMD)

rows: Mid-dilated pupil, high IOP, hazy cornea

sections.title: Critical Red Flags (GCA & Vascular)
content: Scalp tenderness or Jaw claudication (GCA Emergency)
Profound vision loss (NPL/PL) in a white eye (CRAO/GCA)
Bilateral sudden loss (Cortical blindness or GCA)
New onset flashes and floaters (RD/Tear)
Third Nerve Palsy with pupillary involvement (Aneurysm)

sections.title: RAPD Logic: Localizing the Lesion
content: 1. RAPD Present + Clear Media: Optic Nerve (ON) lesion or extensive RD.
2. RAPD Present + Opaque Media: Large RD or Vitreous Heme.
3. RAPD Absent + Dense Vision Loss: Macular pathology or Functional loss.
4. RAPD Absent + Mild Loss: Refractive error or mild Maculopathy.

content.explanation: V: Vascular (CRAO/CRVO/GCA); I: Inflammatory (Optic Neuritis/Uveitis); S: Structural (RD/Heme); I: IOP (AACG); O: Optical (Cornea/Lens changes); N: Neurological (Stroke/Cortex).

sections.title: Immediate Management: CRAO (The 90-Min Window)
content: 1. Digital Massage: Dislodge embolus.
2. IOP Lowering: IV Acetazolamide (500mg) or Paracentesis.
3. Carbogen/Paper Bag: Induce hypercapnia (vasodilation).
4. Immediate Neurology/Stroke Team consultation.
5. Rule out GCA: Stat ESR/CRP if age > 50.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Algorithm
content: Step 1: VA, IOP, and Pupil exam (Check for RAPD).
Step 2: Slit lamp exam (Corneal clarity, AC cells/hypopyon, Gonioscopy).
Step 3: Dilated fundus exam (Look for disc edema, cherry red spot, blood, or RD).
Step 4: If media is hazy (dense cataract/heme), perform B-Scan Ultrasound.
Step 5: Ancillary Imaging: OCT for macula/ONH, FFA for vascular occlusion.
Step 6: Systemic screen: BP, Pulse (A-fib), Carotid auscultation, ESR/CRP.

sections.title: The 'Disc at Risk' (NAION vs AAION)
content: NAION: Painless, sectoral edema, small C/D ratio in fellow eye (disc at risk).
AAION (GCA): Painful (headache), chalky-white edema, systemic malaise.
Clinical Pearl: Every patient >55 with sudden vision loss and disc edema is GCA until proven otherwise.

sections.title: Landmark Studies: The Evidence Base
content: ONTT (Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial): IV methylprednisolone speeds recovery but doesn't change final VA outcome vs placebo.
SCORE/BRAVO/CRUISE: Established anti-VEGF (Ranibizumab/Aflibercept) as gold standard for RVO macular edema.
EAGLE Study: Early lens extraction is superior to LPI for primary angle closure with high IOP.
CVOS (Central Vein Occlusion Study): PRP indicated only when neovascularization develops (360-degree).

sections.title: Surgical Intervention Triggers
content: Rhegmatogenous RD: Immediate surgery (Pars Plana Vitrectomy or Scleral Buckle).
Vitreous Heme with RD: Urgent Vitrectomy.
Non-clearing Vitreous Heme: Elective Vitrectomy after 1-3 months.
Endophthalmitis: Tap and Inject (EVS Study protocols).

sections.title: Recent Advances: The Future of SLOV
content: Tenecteplase for CRAO: Ongoing trials for intra-arterial vs intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5h.
AI-Driven Fundus Screening: Immediate diagnosis of CRVO/CRAO via smartphone imaging.
Neuroprotection: Investigational agents for RGC survival in ischemic events.
